questions.question: Who has the power to regulate the right of citizenship in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Parliament**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The power to regulate the right of citizenship in India is vested in the **Parliament**.
 
• According to the Constitution of India, the Parliament has the authority to make laws regarding the acquisition and termination of citizenship and all other matters related to citizenship.
 
• Article 11 of the Indian Constitution grants Parliament the power to regulate the right of citizenship by law.
 
• Over the years, Parliament has enacted several laws to govern citizenship, including the Citizenship Act of 1955.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The Citizenship Act, 1955** provides for the acquisition and determination of Indian citizenship.
 
• The Act has been amended multiple times, with significant amendments in 1986, 1992, 2003, 2005, and 2019.
 
• Citizenship can be acquired by birth, descent, registration, naturalization, or incorporation of territory.
 
• The Constitution of India, adopted on **26th November 1949** and effective from **26th January 1950**, laid the foundation for the legal framework of citizenship in India.

questions.question: The peninsular plateau of India was a part of which continent earlier?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Africa**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The peninsular plateau of India was once a part of the ancient supercontinent known as Gondwana.
 
• Gondwana included regions that are now part of Africa, South America, Antarctica, Australia, and the Indian subcontinent.
 
• Over millions of years, the tectonic plates drifted apart, leading to the present-day geographical formations.
 
• This separation and movement of the tectonic plates is explained by the theory of continental drift proposed by Alfred Wegener.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The concept of continental drift was further developed into the theory of plate tectonics, which explains the movement of Earth's lithospheric plates.
 
• India's collision with the Eurasian plate led to the formation of the Himalayas.
 
• The peninsular plateau is characterized by its stable geological structure and is one of the oldest landmasses on Earth.
 
• The plateau is rich in minerals and has significant geological and ecological importance.

questions.question: In which year did Johannes Nicolaus Bronsted and Thomas Martin Lowry propose the fundamental concept of acids and bases?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1923**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Johannes Nicolaus Bronsted and Thomas Martin Lowry proposed the fundamental concept of acids and bases in **1923**.
 
• The Bronsted-Lowry theory defines an acid as a proton donor and a base as a proton acceptor.
 
• This theory expanded the understanding of acid-base reactions beyond the limitations of the Arrhenius theory.
 
• It is applicable to a broader range of chemical reactions, including those in non-aqueous solutions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Bronsted-Lowry theory was independently proposed by both scientists in the same year.
 
• This theory is fundamental in the field of chemistry and is widely taught in academic institutions.
 
• The concept of conjugate acid-base pairs is also a significant aspect of the Bronsted-Lowry theory.
 
• Johannes Nicolaus Bronsted was a Danish physical chemist, while Thomas Martin Lowry was a British chemist.

The five-year plans for India with their duration are given below. Which of the following is correctly matched?

 Second five-year plan 
 1956-57 to 1960-61
 
 

 (b)
 Third five-year plan
 1961-62 to 1965-66

 Fourth five-year plan
 1966-67 to 1970-71
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Both a and b**

• **Third Five-Year Plan** (1961-62 to 1965-66): This plan focused on agriculture and improving production to make India self-sufficient in food grains. Hence, b is correctly matched.
 
• **Fourth Five-Year Plan** (1969-74): It aimed at growth with stability and progressive achievement of self-reliance. Note that the given duration (1966-67 to 1970-71) is incorrect. Hence, c is not correctly matched.

__

The first such plan was launched in 1951, and two subsequent five-year plans were formulated until 1965, when there was a break because of the Indo-Pakistan Conflict. The planning process resumed in 1969, after a gap of three annual plans.

questions.question: In which year has India hosted the Asian Games for the first time?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1951**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• India hosted the Asian Games for the first time in the year **1951**.
 
• The inaugural Asian Games were held in New Delhi from March 4 to March 11, 1951.
 
• A total of **489 athletes** from 11 nations participated in the first Asian Games.
 
• The event featured **57 events** across **8 sports** disciplines including athletics, aquatics, basketball, cycling, football, and others.
 
• New Delhi became the first city to host the Asian Games, setting a precedent for future games.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Asian Games, also known as the Asiad, is a continental multi-sport event held every four years among athletes from all over Asia.
 
• The Asian Games are recognized by the International Olympic Committee (IOC) and are described as the second largest multi-sport event after the Olympic Games.
 
• India has hosted the Asian Games twice, first in 1951 and again in 1982, both times in New Delhi.
 
• The Asian Games Federation was the governing body of the Games until it was replaced by the Olympic Council of Asia (OCA) in 1982.
 
• The concept of the Asian Games was first proposed in 1948 during the London Olympic Games by Indian sports official Guru Dutt Sondhi.

questions.question: As of March 2024, who among the following is the Chairperson of the National Green Tribunal?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Prakash Shrivastava**__

__
 
• As of March 2024, **Prakash Shrivastava** is the Chairperson of the National Green Tribunal (NGT).
 
• The National Green Tribunal was established in 2010 under the National Green Tribunal Act for effective and expeditious disposal of cases relating to environmental protection and conservation of forests and other natural resources.
 
• The NGT is tasked with ensuring the enforcement of any legal right relating to the environment and giving relief and compensation for damages to persons and property.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The NGT has a specialized jurisdiction in environmental matters and is guided by principles of natural justice and sustainable development.
 
• It operates across five zones in India: North, Central, East, South, and West, with its principal bench located in New Delhi.
 
• The Tribunal is mandated to dispose of applications or appeals finally within six months of filing.
 
• Previous chairpersons of the NGT include Justice Lokeshwar Singh Panta and Justice Swatanter Kumar.

questions.question: In which part of the Constitution will you find the six broad categories of Fundamental Rights?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Part III**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Part III** of the Constitution of India deals with Fundamental Rights.
 
• These rights are considered essential for the overall development of individuals and are enforceable by the courts.
 
• The six broad categories of Fundamental Rights include the right to equality, the right to freedom, the right against exploitation, the right to freedom of religion, cultural and educational rights, and the right to constitutional remedies.
 
• Fundamental Rights are meant to protect individuals from any arbitrary actions by the state and ensure a fair and just society.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Constitution of India was adopted by the Constituent Assembly on **26th November 1949** and **came into effect on 26th January 1950**.
 
• It lays down the framework defining fundamental political principles, establishes the structure, procedures, powers, and duties of government institutions, and sets out fundamental rights, directive principles, and the duties of citizens.
 
• The Constitution of India is the longest written constitution of any country in the world.
 
• It declares India a sovereign, socialist, secular, and democratic republic, assuring its citizens justice, equality, and liberty, and endeavors to promote fraternity.
 
• Amendments to the Constitution can be made through a process outlined in **Article 368**.
 
• The Fundamental Rights have been amended several times to address the changing needs and aspirations of the people.

questions.question: Geoid is the ______ of earth.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**shape**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **geoid** is the **shape** that the surface of the Earth's oceans would take under the influence of Earth's gravity and rotation alone, disregarding other influences such as winds and tides.
 
• It is an equipotential surface of the Earth's gravitational field, which means that it is a surface on which the gravitational potential is constant.
 
• The geoid is used as a reference surface from which to measure the elevation of geographical features.
 
• It is often described as the true physical figure of the Earth, as opposed to a simplified mathematical model like an ellipsoid.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The geoid concept was first introduced by the German mathematician and astronomer **Johann Benedikt Listing** in 1873.
 
• The geoid is irregular, but it can be approximated by a mathematical model known as an ellipsoid of revolution.
 
• Modern satellite geodesy techniques are used to measure the geoid with high precision.
 
• Understanding the geoid is crucial for various fields such as oceanography, geophysics, and civil engineering.

questions.question: How many squares are there on a chessboard?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**64**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A standard **chessboard** is an **8x8 grid**, making it a total of **64 squares**.
 
• The chessboard is used for the game of **chess**, which is a **two-player strategy board game**.
 
• Each player begins with **16 pieces**: one king, one queen, two rooks, two knights, two bishops, and eight pawns.
 
• The objective of the game is to **checkmate** the opponent's king, which means putting the king in a position where it cannot escape capture.
 
• The **64 squares** alternate in color, typically **black and white** or **dark and light**.
 
• Each square on the board is identified by a unique **coordinate** from a1 to h8.
 
• The game of chess is believed to have originated in **India** during the **Gupta Empire** in the **6th century AD**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **chessboard** is a key component in the game of chess, which is recognized as a **global intellectual sport**.
 
• **Chess** is governed by the **International Chess Federation (FIDE)**, which sets the rules and organizes world championships.
 
• The game has a rich history and has been a part of various cultures and societies around the world.
 
• **Chess** is not only a game but also used as a tool for **educational purposes**, improving **cognitive skills** and **strategic thinking**.
 
• **64 squares** also symbolize the **mathematical precision** required in the game, reflecting the **importance of planning** and **foresight**.
